title: Half-Term Days Out: A School Holiday Planner for Families
description: Plan half-term and school holiday days out without the stress or the peak prices: when to book, how to beat crowds, rainy-day backups and real ways to save.
h1: Half-term days out: your school holiday planner
intro: School holidays are when everyone wants a day out, and when prices and queues peak. A little planning keeps the fun high and the cost down.

image.alt: A child in yellow wellies walking through autumn leaves

keywords: things to do in half term
cardText: When to book, how to dodge the crowds and how to keep half-term costs down.

blocks.title: Scout’s half-term plan
blocks.text: Mix one “big” paid day with two or three free or cheap ones. Book the big day early and keep a rainy-day backup in your pocket.
points: Check term dates for your area: they differ between councils and schools
Book timed tickets as soon as you know your dates
Plan a free day for the middle of the week

sections.html: Term dates vary between councils, academies and private schools, so two families on the same street can have different half-terms. Find yours on GOV.UK (England) or your council’s website. In the US, spring break and winter break also vary by school district.

Popular attractions like the Harry Potter Studio Tour and big theme parks sell timed tickets that can go weeks ahead for holiday dates. Most use date-based pricing, so the earlier you book, the more choice you have.

• Go midweek: Tuesdays to Thursdays are usually quieter than Mondays and Fridays.
  • Arrive at opening: the first hour is the calmest at almost every attraction.
  • Avoid the first weekend: it’s often the busiest of the holiday.

• Use 2FOR1 with the train where it’s available.
  • Fill gaps with free days out like national museums and country parks.
  • Take a picnic: see our picnic checklist.
  • Check kids-go-free offers before paying for little ones.
Keep one indoor idea ready for the inevitable wet day: an aquarium, a museum, a swimming pool or a cinema morning. Our rainy day days out list has plenty.
Autumn half-term is perfect for pumpkin picking and Halloween events, crunchy woodland walks and theme park Halloween seasons. Check whether events need separate tickets.

faqs.a: It depends on your local authority or school. In England, check GOV.UK or your council’s website. Many schools have a week off in late October, mid-February and late May.

faqs.q: How can I make half-term cheaper?
faqs.a: Book paid attractions early and midweek, mix in free days out, use rail 2FOR1 offers and kids-go-free deals, and take a picnic.
